newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Tatneft to shed non-core units.
newsitem.headline: Russian Tatneft to shed non-core units.

text.p: Russian independent oil company AO Tatneft has begun a restructuring programme aimed at disposing of non-core businesses and slashing its workforce, its public relations company Glashatai said on Tuesday.

"The basic job (of the firm) is oil production, but service and auxiliary activities will be transferred or sold to subsidiary companies and private licensed companies which are based on former Tatneft divisions," Glashatai quoted Tatneft chief executive Rinat Galeyev as saying.
He said the reorganisation of the independent producer, based on Western models, envisaged shedding 35-40 percent of the 75,000-strong workforce and was due to be completed in 1998.

When the Tartastan government, one of the company's biggest shareholders, gave the go-ahead for the restructuring in February last year, Tatneft was an industrial and social group made up of 139 subsidiaries and employing over 75,000 people.

Galeyev said five communal farms, 83 kindergartens, 624,000 square metres of living space and sports and cultural centres had already been handed over to local authorities, while agricultural units had started to work as private companies.
"Companies formerly belonging to us will be able to broaden the sphere of their activities, which will protect and expand the number of jobs," Galeyev said.
The restructuring is a bold move for a company in Russia, where most enterprises support, at a loss, a large number of non-core businesses left over from the Soviet planned economy.
Last year Tatneft produced 23.70 million tonnes of oil, excluding joint venture output, down slightly from 1995 levels of 24.14 million tonnes.
Tatneft is a regional oil company with crude oil production but no refineries.

The government of Russia's autonomous republic of Tatarstan owns 32 percent of the company and employees and management hold 41.34 percent. In December it placed 10 percent of its capital in the form of American Depositary Shares.
